stem.text: Some vaccines do not contain antigens. The vaccines contain a molecule of mRNA. Cells in the immune system use the mRNA molecule to make a protein antigen.
The statements describe the stages of how mRNA vaccines work when they enter a cell of the immune system.

items: B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes with complementary receptors bind to the protein.
Lymphocytes differentiate into memory cells that give long lasting immunity.
Ribosomes translate the mRNA molecule to make a protein.
The cell displays the protein on its cell surface membrane.
